items.text: Who owns Canada's economy?
items.article: Mark Carney is asking the world to invest in Canada. But who already owns Canada? And what would more foreign investment mean for our sovereignty? Prime Minister Mark Carney has been working to bring more foreign investment into Canada. At his recent Investment Summit, he told investors from all over the world that Canada “has what the world wants." This got us wondering, who already owns Canada's businesses and infrastructure? And could that change now that the government is courting more outside investment? Earlier this year, Marc Lee, a senior economist with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives, wrote a piece called “Masters in our own house”, where he looked at how much of our economy is owned by foreign entities. He talks about what a new wave of foreign investment means for our sovereignty. items.text: Carole Middleton's strict demand for Prince William that keeps him down to earth
items.article: He might be the heir to the throne, but that doesn't excuse the Prince of Wales from helping out around the house whenever he's staying with Michael and Carole Middleton Growing up in royalty, Prince William will have had servants to tend to his every need, whether it was clearing the table, preparing a meal or even taking the bins out. However, whenever the Prince of Wales is visiting his in-laws, Michael and Carole Middleton , it appears that the heir to the throne is put to work just like any other member of the family. Speaking on True Royalty TV, Russell Myers, the royal editor of the Daily Mirror, revealed how William helps out with Carole. "I remember being told by close friends of the Middletons how there were no airs and graces," he said. "If he was staying, he was mucking in, laying the table. He was helping make the Sunday dinner. If he was lying on the sofa with his feet up, Carole will give him a nudge and tell him to take the bins out." However, none of this bothers William, with Russell explaining: "That is exactly how they treated him, and he absolutely loved it." William has always been close to Michael and Carole , and the pair couldn't contain their joy when it was confirmed that William was engaged to their daughter, the now Princess of Wales .

items.text: Here's all the free money Trump's talked about giving Americans during his second term — and where it all stands
items.article: From tariff rebate checks, to bonuses, to Trump accounts, to DOGE dividends, here's all the free money Trump has floated giving to Americans. President Donald Trump really wants to send you a check. Throughout his second term, Trump has pledged to send Americans money in various ways, including tariff rebate checks and bonuses to select government employees. Some of that free money is actually becoming a reality: Congress created "Trump Accounts" as part of the "Big Beautiful Bill," which will provide tax-free federal grants of $1,000 to children born in the next few years. Others remain elusive, or have fallen by the wayside. Remember the DOGE dividend ? Trump also sent out checks during his first term, but under much different circumstances. As part of two successive COVID-era stimulus bills, the federal government sent Americans $1,200 in the spring of 2020 and $600 in the winter, shortly before the president left office. Trump's signature appeared on those checks, which was a source of controversy during a presidential election year.

items.key: ai:claudia winkleman will never take part in celebrity traitors for one reason
items.text: Claudia Winkleman will never take part in Celebrity Traitors for one reason
items.article: Celebrity Traitors host Claudia Winkleman loves hosting the hit BBC show but has made it abundantly clear you'll never see her appearing in the castle as a contestant Claudia Winkleman reckons she is "too thick" to take part in the Celebrity Traitors as a contestant. The beloved TV presenter hosts The Traitors as well as the celebrity spin-off, the latter of which will return to screens on Thursday (October 1) with a brand new batch of famous faces. The second series will air at 8pm on BBC One and iPlayer. Actors Michael Sheen and Richard E Grant, supermodel Jerry Hall, Maya Jama and comics Rob Beckett, Romesh Ranganathan and James Acaster are in the line-up, alongside Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock, James Blunt and The Last Of Us star Bella Ramsey. However, Claudia said she would never want to compete on the programme as she'd be "awful" at the game. She said: "I'm too thick. I mustn't play it in public. I must not, thank you so much. "I'm just being honest. I could have come up with a schmoozier (answer) but no. It's a privilege to play that game and to be at the round table, but I think I would just be too awful at it." The first celebrity spin-off was won by traitor Alan Carr. Executive producer Sarah Fay said she was "chuffed" the series was such a hit and hopes the second one lives up to the past success and even ups the ante.

items.article: Suraag: The Clue premiered on DD National in June 1999 and ran successfully for four years. Its final episode aired in November 2002. If you are a 80s or 90s kid, we are sure you grew up watching Doordarshan and are surely aware that Suraag: The Clue remains one of the most remembered crime-investigation shows of its time. Nearly 27 years after the original series premiered, the popular detective drama has now made a comeback with Suraag 2.0. The new series brings back the familiar world of crime, investigation and clues, but introduces a new generation of characters and a more contemporary storytelling format. The revival comes from Sri Adhikari Brothers in association with Doordarshan, and the makers are calling it a re-imagination rather than a straightforward remake of the original. Here’s everything about Suraag 2.0 you must know: Suraag: The Clue premiered on DD National in June 1999 and ran successfully for four years. Its final episode aired in November 2002. The series reportedly had 174 episodes. In the original Suraag, Sudesh Berry played Inspector Bharat, a Delhi CID officer known for his unconventional approach to solving complicated cases. Amit Kapoor played Inspector Srivastava, his associate in the show. Each episode generally revolved around a crime, an investigation and the eventual discovery of the clues that helped solve the mystery. items.key: ai:this under-the-radar region is having a 'quiet wine' boom. here's why
items.text: This under-the-radar region is having a ‘quiet wine’ boom. Here’s why
items.article: Hungary's Tokaj was designated a wine region nearly 300 years ago, with winemaking dating back nearly 1,000 years. Mention European wine, and you'll likely picture the grand châteaux of Bordeaux or the rolling hills of Chianti as the ultimate destinations for vineyard tours. But travel further east, and you'll reach Hungary's Tokaj area, which — like Chianti — is one of the world's oldest officially demarcated wine-growing regions. Global wine exports were down 4.7% in volume between 2024 and 2025, according to the International Organisation of Vine and Wine (OIV), but Tokaj appears to be bucking the trend in something of a "quiet wine" boom. The region's production rose 8% to 10% over the same period, according to tourism board Visit Tokaj. Tokaj — less than three hours by train from Hungary's capital, Budapest — was classified as a wine region nearly 300 years ago, with winemaking going back nearly 1,000 years. Indeed, King Louis XIV of France declared the region's sweet Tokaji Aszú wine as: "The wine of kings and the king of wines," after receiving a shipment to the Palace of Versailles as a diplomatic gift from a Hungarian prince in the 1700s. Centuries later, it remains the Tokaj region's signature wine, produced from furmint white grapes that thrive in the area and are naturally affected by Botrytis cinerea — or noble rot — in a process that concentrates the fruit's sugars, according to Visit Tokaj's Dale Takio. The iPhone Air remains a premium package with a slim 5.6mm form factor, making it a rather appealing device to use. For performance, you get the A19 Pro chipset on the iPhone Air. In our review, the device can handle multitasking quite effectively.

items.text: Six authentic Spanish restaurants in the UK you need to know about
items.article: From Bermondsey tapas counters to Basque grills in Cardiff, there's a spot for every occasion Whether it’s tasty tapas, a perfect paella or the finest Rioja, you’ll find Spanish food and culture at its best in these British eateries Discover certified, authentic Spanish restaurants across the UK, offering everything from lively pintxos bars to Basque-inspired grills Credit: Asador 44 The UK is home to some outstanding Spanish cuisine. From city hotspots that make you feel you’re in a bustling San Sebastian pintxos bar to upscale Catalonian-inspired eateries specialising in seafood, there’s a place for every kind of budget and occasion. When deciding where to book, the trick is to choose a restaurant that not only comes highly recommended, but also bears the official Restaurants from Spain certification . These restaurants are not only pioneers of Spanish gastronomy, but they are also some of the best in the UK. With its counter seating, open kitchen, and no bookings policy, this small but mighty Bermondsey tapas bar with a Michelin Bib Gourmand tucked under its belt is led by renowned chef José Pizarro, and captures the essence of traditional Spanish neighbourhood bars. Huddle around the countertop to enjoy small plates, Iberian ham and delicious seafood. It’s bustling, lively and the perfect place for meeting with friends. The chalkboard specials are always worth exploring, while the acorn-fed jamón ibérico , pan con tomate , croquetas and Padrón peppers all rate highly
